<reason>A better established the relevant comparison: the additional deals stricter enforcement would block, not harmful mergers generally. B supplied a plausible high-risk filter but inadequately defended its assumptions that alternative commercialization remains available and blocking costs are temporary. A answered both pressure questions directly and correctly challenged B’s exclusion of productivity savings unless passed through to consumers. B’s closing also overstated A’s concession: uncertain pass-through does not establish that remaining competition disappears or that stricter blocking produces net benefits.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A undermined B’s central asymmetry between permanent merger harms and temporary blocking costs: losing financing or a development window can prevent a product from reaching market altogether. B’s closing repeated that scale could be rebuilt elsewhere without resolving this objection.</best_rebuttal>
